reason: Connecting the brain and spinal cord seems like a useful starting point for the command route.
expectation: I expect a central pathway that can later connect sight and muscle commands.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the eyes to sensory nerves also supports the goal, but I chose to start with the central pathway.

effect: The brain and spinal cord now form the central nervous system; I still need to connect sight and muscle commands.
reaction: The result was expected and made the central route clearer.
reason: Connecting the eyes to sensory nerves should establish the incoming sight pathway.
expectation: I expect a pathway carrying visual information from the eyes, though it may still need to connect to the central nervous system.

alternatives.reason: The motor nerves should connect the arm to outgoing commands, but I chose to establish the sight pathway first.

effect: The eyes and sensory nerves now form a visual information route, which can connect to the central nervous system.
reaction: The change from light rays to a nerve signal is clear and interesting.
reason: Connecting the visual route to the central nervous system advances the sight-to-command goal.
expectation: I expect visual information to reach the central nervous system; the arm's motor connection may still need to be made.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the motor nerves to the arm also advances the goal, but I want to finish the incoming route first.

effect: Visual signals now reach the brain, identifying the target, but the arm still needs an outgoing command route.
reaction: The distinction between seeing the target and producing movement is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should connect motor signals to the arm muscles.
expectation: I expect the arm to gain a motor nerve connection that may still need to link to the control system.

effect: The arm now has outgoing nerves connected to its muscles, ready to link with the seeing control system.
reaction: The branching nerves make the command route clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should connect sight with commands to the arm.
expectation: I expect the control system to connect to the arm so it can direct movement toward the visible target.

effect: The guided arm connects visual input to outgoing muscle commands, and the new goal calls for position feedback.
reaction: The two arrow directions make the connection clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and stretch receptors appear suited to reporting the arm's position.
expectation: I expect the receptors and sensory nerves to provide information about muscle stretch back to the control system.

effect: The completed arm now sends position information back to the central nervous system, showing how it can be guided without watching it.
reaction: The eyes-closed example made the role of position feedback especially clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding position feedback was most worthwhile because the eyes-closed example connected the sensors to an experience I can recognize.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the brain and spinal cord was straightforward, but its result added little explanation beyond naming the central nervous system.

surprise.text: The position sensors helped me think about how the arm can be guided without relying entirely on sight.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary: the offered combinations followed the goal, although several were the only available choice.

continue.text: I would be somewhat interested in continuing to see how the guided arm is used, though the sequence became predictable once only one combination was offered.
